comparisons.D12: For p>2 define A0=max((p^2-p-2+(p-2)*sqrt(p^2+10*p+1))/(4*p),1), then require A>A0 strictly. The radicand is positive and denominator nonzero on this domain, so real square-root and division defaults do not affect the intended value. Keep both the -p-2 numerator term and the denominator 4*p, which distinguish this cutoff from A0-prime in (2.10). This is a numeric condition used by Theorems2.2 and2.4, not a proof that the Gaussian approximation holds or an additional nonsingularity condition inherited merely by referencing its formula.

comparisons.D13: For p>2 define A0_prime=max((p^2-4+(p-2)*sqrt(p^2+20*p+4))/(8*p),1), and retain A>A0_prime. Its denominator is 8*p and its radicand is p^2+20*p+4, unlike the separate cutoff (2.7). rows.gap: The uniform constants and admissible nonempty block ranges must be supplied to state the condition with its exact block length.

comparisons.D11: Choose c>0 and an integer l0 uniformly, then for each admissible sample size n and l with l>=l0 and 1<=l<=n require every j=1,...,n-l+1 to satisfy norm_L2(sum_(r=j)^(j+l-1) X_r)^2/l>=c. This block contains exactly l terms. The source leaves n implicit in the displayed condition; preserve the nonempty-block domain rather than assigning a minimum to an empty range or a reciprocal at l=0. On mean-zero square-integrable processes this norm squared is the block variance, but finite second moments must be checked before converting extended L2 values to reals. The bound grows at least linearly with l; it is stronger than mere divergence of minimal block second moments and says nothing about independence or stationarity.

comparisons.D10: For the fixed total n and p>2, set b=n^(1/p) and X_i_plus=max(min(X_i,b),-b) for every i=1,...,n. Form S_i_plus by summing X_j_plus minus ITS OWN expectation from j=1 through i. This is winsorization/clipping, not deletion of observations exceeding b, and E[X_j]=0 does not imply the clipped mean is zero. The threshold uses total sample size n rather than the running index i. Bounded clipping gives integrability on a probability space, so the center is well-defined. Preserve the distinction between covariance of uncentered clipped variables and second moments of their centered partial sums, as used in the separate approximation statements.

comparisons.D15: Set zeta1=min(1,2-4/p)/(1+2*A) with p>2 and A>1, and take positive integer m comparable to n^zeta1, using upper and lower constant bounds or two IsBigO relations. This uses min rather than max and includes the boundary p=4 correctly. The exponent is positive and less than one, consistent with growing sublinear blocks, but a concrete integer rounding still needs its comparability proof. The subsequent prose compares it to zeta2=min(1,2-4/p)/3 with a reversed printed inequality: for A>1 the formulas actually give zeta1<zeta2. Preserve the formula and source issue rather than copying that reversed comparison. Referencing zeta1 in Theorem3.2 does not import conditional bootstrap O_(P*) assumptions or the BRV estimator.

comparisons.D17: On [0,1], take the stated probability density f with three continuous derivatives and F(t)=integral_0^t f. With the positive lower bound used in Theorem4.1, F is strictly increasing and maps endpoints to 0 and1, so an ordinary inverse on [0,1] can define t_i=F_inverse(i/n). Merely being a nonnegative smooth density would permit flat portions and require a generalized inverse convention. The source first imposes t_n<t_(n+1)=1, but for the positive-density quantile formula t_n=F_inverse(1)=1, violating that strict inequality. Retain both printed statements and the unresolved endpoint convention; do not silently change i/n to i/(n+1) or drop the last observation. The grid is deterministic design, not empirical sample quantiles.

comparisons.D9: For EVERY integer sequence m_n tending to infinity with m_n<n, take the minimum over i=1,...,n-m_n of norm_L2(X_i+...+X_(i+m_n)) squared and require it tend to positive infinity. Each block contains m_n+1 terms, unlike the length-l blocks in Condition2.4. The minimum is over a nonempty finite set under m_n<n; keep the positive sample-size domain explicit. Quantification over all diverging admissible sequences is stronger than checking one convenient sequence. This condition asserts divergence only and does not supply a uniform c times block length lower bound. Finite second moments and zero means determine when the squared L2 norm can be identified with variance; no independence is added.

comparisons.D6: For each nonnegative integer i sum the uniform functional-dependence coefficients delta_p(k) from k=i through infinity, including the first lag i. The coefficient already takes a supremum over observation time; do not move this supremum outside the tail sum or sum the individual time-specific effects first. Reindex by k=i+r for r in N. A nonnegative ENNReal sum retains possible divergence, and summable_toReal applies only once the total is known finite. comparisons.D7: Retain the causal process (1.2), p>2, Theta_(0,p)<infinity, some A>1 and a finite positive C such that every i>=0 satisfies (i+1)^A*Theta_(i,p)<=C. Because the weighted values form a nonempty bounded-above real set after finiteness is established, csSup_le_iff identifies this all-lag bound with the printed supremum mu_(p,A)<=C. The weight is (i+1)^A and applies to the TAIL sum, not merely delta_p(i). Do not replace the uniform bound by a limit at infinity, an eventual bound without handling initial lags, or a time-averaged condition. No covariance nonsingularity assumption is included in this dependence condition, and the term norm does not by itself supply a library normed-space instance.

comparisons.D14: Use Q_n=sum over 1<=s<=t<=n of a_(s,t)*X_s*X_t with |a_(s,t)|<=1 and a_(s,t)=0 for |s-t|>D_n. The sums and ceiling require a positive INTEGER D_n<=n, although the display only explicitly states D_n<=n. For k=1,...,ceil(n/D_n), group terms by t from (k-1)*D_n+1 to min(k*D_n,n), and for each such t sum all s=1,...,t; the band constraint automatically removes distant terms. R_k is the sum of V_j-E[V_j] for j<=k, not the leftover linear block variable R_j defined earlier in (3.1). Do not symmetrize the upper triangular sum into a full matrix product without half-weighting off-diagonal entries, or count those products twice. Dependence across blocks is allowed; finite second moments ensure each product expectation exists.

comparisons.D18: Take a smooth symmetric real kernel supported in [-omega,omega]. For each delta>=0 and u, define Psi_K(u;delta) as the supremum of |K(y)-K(u)| for |y-u|<=delta, including both endpoints. The constraint set contains y=u, and continuity on the compact neighborhood bounds the values, so the real supremum is meaningful; measurability/integrability of the resulting modulus still needs justification. Express integral_R Psi_K(u;delta) du=O(delta) as delta tends to zero THROUGH POSITIVE values, not through negative radii with empty neighborhoods. Smooth compact support is a route to this bound, but the predicate should match the displayed integrated modulus. The source does not separately state integral K=1 or nondegeneracy of the local-linear denominator; do not add these as if quoted or infer that this kernel condition alone settles them.
